title: Irrevocability of an offer
summary: Irrevocability means that an offeror’s attempted withdrawal cannot terminate the protected power of acceptance during the applicable period.
notes:
An irrevocable offer does not itself mean the offeree has accepted, owes performance, or may wait forever. Different sources supply different conditions and durations of protection. Compare a paid option, UCC § 2-205, beginning performance under Restatement § 45, and reliance in Drennan. The full entries preserve the requirements of each route and the limits on delay or renewed bargaining.

Add separate notes for an option supported by consideration, reliance, beginning invited performance, and firm offers. Drennan supplies the reliance example here.
